key_insight: Later-generation OpenAI configurations showed higher emergency sensitivity, but no system performed best across all urgency categories.
clinical_relevance: Self-triage evaluation should assess emergency recognition separately from overall agreement, since the highest-agreement model had the lowest emergency sensitivity.
method: Compared study-specific SmED and Infermedica implementations with five structured OpenAI configurations.
Used an LLM patient actor across 480 physician-curated vignettes derived from German routine triage data.
Compared three-category urgency recommendations against preliminary physician consensus using routine-frequency-derived weights.
evidence_signal: Weighted emergency sensitivity ranged from 51.3% to 99.9%, while weighted exact three-category agreement ranged from 54.4% to 68.8%.
watch_item: Preliminary consensus and study-specific implementations limit generalizability; the comparison does not establish longitudinal accuracy improvement or evaluate the manufacturers’ certified products directly.
paper_title: Benchmark Self-Triage (BeST): Comparing Self-Triage Systems and Multiple Generations of OpenAI Models Against Preliminary Expert Consensus
